Describe how the keys of two tables match

Source: R/describe_match.R
describe_match.Rd

Before a join, the question is what it will do: how many keys are in both tables, how many rows will find no match, and whether the other table repeats a key and so multiplies rows. describe_match() counts the keys found in both tables, only in data and only in reference, with the rows they stand for, and says how many rows a left join of data to reference returns. It judges nothing; require a match with ensure_matched().

Usage

describe_match(data, reference, by)

Arguments

data

A data frame or tibble, or a database or Arrow table: see Database tables in checkpoints.

reference

A reference data frame or database/Arrow table. For database input, a local reference is sent as an inline query; remote references must be on the same connection. Local input requires a local reference. No table is written to the database.

by

Character vector of key columns, optionally named to map names in data to names in reference, e.g. c(cpr = "person_id"). Required: no implicit natural join is performed.

Value

An object of class inshape_match, printed as a summary. It is a list with by (the key columns of reference, named by those of data), the counts n_rows and n_ref_rows, n_missing and n_ref_missing (rows with a missing key), n_ref_dup_keys (keys occurring more than once in reference) and n_join_rows (the rows of a left join of data to reference), and a tibble keys with one row for each of "in both", "only in data" and "only in reference": keys (distinct keys), rows (the rows of data with those keys) and ref_rows (the rows of reference).

Details

A key with a missing value in any of its columns matches nothing, as with na_matches = "never" in ensure_matched(): those rows are counted on their own and kept out of the keys. A left join keeps each of them once.

Key columns are compared as they are. An integer and a double column match, and so do a factor and a character column; other pairs of different types, such as a number against text, stop with an error rather than match nothing. In a database the comparison is the database's own: DuckDB refuses a number against text as well, with its own error.

See also

ensure_matched() to require that every key is found and see the rows, describe_key() for the duplicated keys of one table, describe_changes() to compare two extracts of the same register.

Examples

income <- data.frame(
  cpr    = c("a", "a", "b", "c", NA),
  year   = c(2023, 2024, 2024, 2024, 2024),
  income = c(10, 12, 7, 9, 3)
)
persons <- data.frame(
  person_id = c("a", "b", "b", "d"),
  kommune   = c("955", "956", "957", "960")
)
# c is not in the register, d has no income, and b is there twice, so
# the join returns one row more than income has
describe_match(income, persons, by = c(cpr = "person_id"))
#> ── Match: cpr = person_id ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> data: 5 rows, reference: 4 rows
#> 
#> ⚠ Rows of data without a match: 2 (40.0%), 1 of them with a missing key
#> ⚠ Keys repeated in the reference: 1; a left join returns 6 rows, 1 more than data
#> 
#> Keys:
#>     found              keys  rows ref_rows
#>   1 in both               2     3        3
#>   2 only in data          1     1        0
#>   3 only in reference     1     0        1
